ra1.[note 1]: All figures are net of sales, fees and charges, and net of transfers between local authorities and from other delivery bodies.
ra1.[note 2]: Expenditure funded by the NHS, such as through the Better Care Fund, is excluded.
ra1.[note 3]: The financing elements do not sum exactly to the Revenue expenditure total (a difference of £187million, which equates to 0.1% of revenue Expenditure). This occurs as a result of the estimation for the authorities from which we had received no data; this grossing up to England figures is necessarily done separately to the grossing for all expenditure figures, and a slight mismatch is expected.
ra1.[note 4]: Seven authorities have provided council tax figures that materially differ from figures reported in their CTR return. No explanation for this discrepancy has been provided.
ra1.[note 5]: Several grants have been consolidated into the Revenue Support Grant for 2026-27 resulting in a large increase in this grant value from the previous financial year and a reduction in the value of specific and special grants.
ra1.[note 6]: Only 22 eligible local authorities have reported values for the High Needs Stability Grant. Where the grant has been reflected, authorities have taken differing approaches to earmarking the funding, including treatment through the DSG adjustment account, DSG reserves, or other earmarked reserves. These differences in recording practices reduce the comparability of reserve balances and appropriations between authorities. In particular, users should exercise caution when interpreting figures relating to the DSG adjustment account, DSG reserves and associated appropriations, as they may not consistently reflect planned High Needs Stability Grant funding.
ra1.[note 7]: A number of changes to the business rates retention system were introduced for 2026-27 as part of the Fair Funding Review 2.0. Users should consider these changes when making comparisons with previous years at an England, class, or local authority level.
ra1.[note 8]: Changes to business rates in the 2026-27 financial year have meant that some authorities submitted positive figures to represent a collection fund deficit in excess of their 2026-27 retained value.
ra1.[x]: RA return not received in time for publication.
ra1.M: RA return not received in time for publication. England totals have been estimated by also drawing on grant allocations, where known, or the proportions within the previous year's data.
ra1.[o]: Class total estimates are a new development. Their introduction follows the switch to a grossing methodology in 2023 to calculate England estimates. Starting with RA2024-25, grossed (estimated) figures are calculated for each class of local authority, and the results summed to make the grossed England total.

ra2.[note 1]: Six authorities have reported negative DSG reserves levels following advice from auditors.
ra2.[note 2]: Eight authorities have reported negative schools reserves levels as a result of the statutory override being recorded in the wrong place.
ra2.[note 3]: The 2026-27 RA form has split how HRA depreciation and debt is recorded into two new lines (RA4026 and RA4027), this has impacted how authorities record their HRA figures on the following lines.
ra2.[note 4]: Due to the differing approaches that have been taken by the 22 eligible local authorities who have reported values for the High Needs Stability Grant, users should exercise caution when interpreting figures relating to the DSG adjustment account, DSG reserves and associated appropriations, as they do not consistently reflect planned High Needs Stability Grant funding. For more details, see the annex of this report.
